evals.prompt: Using the REST API, create a Geti detection project, upload an image, annotate it, and start training.
evals.expected_output: An end-to-end REST workflow that creates and verifies the project, uploads and annotates media, submits an asynchronous training job, tracks it to completion, and verifies the trained model.
expectations: Asks for the Geti instance base URL and uses `/api/openapi.json` as the authoritative source for request payloads instead of assuming a fixed deployment URL
Orders the REST workflow as project creation, media upload, annotation, and training job submission
Submits training through `POST /api/jobs` with job type `train` rather than treating training as a synchronous endpoint
Tracks the job through `GET /api/jobs/<id>` or the job status/log streams and verifies the resulting model under the project
Stays at the REST API usage layer and does not propose backend implementation changes

evals.prompt: Configure a source, model, and sink for my Geti project, enable live inference, and tell me how to verify that it is running.
evals.expected_output: A REST workflow that creates or identifies source and sink resources, wires them with a model into the project pipeline, enables it, and verifies active inference through pipeline state and metrics.
expectations: Creates or identifies source and sink resources and selects an existing trained model before enabling the pipeline
Uses `PATCH /api/projects/<id>/pipeline` to bind the source, model, and sink
Uses `POST /api/projects/<id>/pipeline:enable` only after the three pipeline components are configured
Verifies the configured pipeline and checks `/api/projects/<id>/pipeline/metrics` for latency or throughput
Mentions the disable operation or another concrete recovery action without suggesting backend code changes
